home.title: Coral restoration,
home.intro: Learn about the coral life cycle and support its recovery through care, monitoring, and collaboration.
home.fact1: The process begins with the responsible selection and collection of coral fragments.
home.fact2: Fragments are prepared and placed in structures that support growth and monitoring.
home.fact3: Cleaning, maintenance, and monitoring take place throughout their development.
home.processHeading: Restoration takes time, care, and knowledge.
home.reefIntro: The cycle includes gametes, embryo, larva, settlement on substrate, juvenile coral, and adult coral.
home.ctaText: Learn about the place, the process, and the coral life cycle.

content.locationDescription: In this area, coral collection, planting, monitoring, and maintenance activities help study development and contribute to reef recovery.
howWeWork: Responsible selection and collection of coral fragments.
Preparing and placing fragments in marine nurseries and structures designed to support growth.
Cleaning, maintaining, and monitoring corals and water conditions.
content.whyRestore: Reefs provide homes and shelter for many marine species, help protect coastlines, and are part of the lives of communities that depend on the sea.
content.collaboration: Restoring a reef requires knowledge and collaboration. Researchers, institutions, and communities work together to care for corals, learn from them, and bring life back to affected areas.
